title: Secure Token Pruning Mechanism and Accelerator for Vision Transformer
problem: Vision Transformers are vulnerable to adversarial patch attacks; existing defense strategies improve robustness but incur significant computational overhead, limiting practical deployment in security-critical applications.
motivation: Secure ViT deployment in critical applications requires efficient adversarial robustness; combining defense with efficiency enables edge deployment without sacrificing security.
method: STEM defense integrates Block-wise Selective Fusion (BSF) to fuse redundant and flag suspicious tokens, and Identify-Prune (IP) to remove adversarial tokens based on multi-head attention statistics. STEMA accelerator features dedicated Security Core with token fusion, top-k selection, and metadata engines (5% chip area).
key_novelty: Parallelizable token pruning defense combining selective fusion and statistical pruning with dedicated hardware accelerator occupying minimal chip area.
contributions: 4.7× robustness improvement vs. token pruning methods
limitations: Evaluation limited to vision tasks; threat model scope unclear; applicability to other Transformer architectures not discussed.
primary_theme: Secure and efficient Vision Transformer acceleration
